blocks.text: PCA found directions of greatest variance within the covariance matrix, but left one genuine detail unstated, the exact mathematical operation scikit-learn actually uses to compute those directions underneath. SVD, Singular Value Decomposition, is that genuine operation directly, and it turns out to be a considerably more general, powerful tool than PCA alone, one PCA is really just one specific, common application of.

This topic covers how SVD genuinely decomposes any matrix at all into three component matrices, how PCA is genuinely just SVD applied to mean centered data, how to interpret the singular values this decomposition produces, a real, genuine advantage SVD has for sparse data specifically, directly connecting back to the TF-IDF matrices from Text Features, and Latent Semantic Analysis, a well known, named application of this exact technique to text.
1. Decomposing Any Matrix Into Three Pieces

blocks.alt: Any matrix decomposes into U, Sigma, and V transpose

blocks.text: SVD genuinely takes any matrix at all, not just a covariance matrix, and decomposes it into three separate matrices, U, a genuine matrix of left singular vectors, Sigma, a genuine diagonal matrix of singular values, and V transpose, a genuine matrix of right singular vectors. Multiplying these three matrices back together genuinely reconstructs the original matrix exactly.

This is genuinely a far more general operation than PCA, it works directly on the raw data matrix itself, with no requirement to first compute a covariance matrix at all, a real, practical difference covered directly in the sections that follow.
2. PCA Is Genuinely Just SVD on Centered Data

blocks.alt: SVD on centered data produces the same result as PCA

blocks.text: When a data matrix is genuinely mean centered first, subtracting each feature own average from every value, exactly the first step of standardization covered back in Standardization, applying SVD directly to that centered matrix produces genuinely the exact same principal components PCA would produce through the covariance matrix route.

This is genuinely worth holding onto directly, PCA and SVD are not two separate, competing techniques, PCA is genuinely just one specific, common use case of the more general SVD operation, applied specifically to mean centered data.

blocks.text: 3. Reading the Singular Values

blocks.alt: A large singular value marks an important direction while a small one marks a minor direction

blocks.text: The singular values sitting along Sigma genuine diagonal directly indicate how much real, meaningful structure each corresponding direction captures, closely paralleling the eigenvalues and explained variance covered back in PCA. A genuinely large singular value means that direction captures real, substantial structure in the data, a genuinely small one means that direction captures comparatively little.

This gives SVD the genuine same practical capability PCA offered, ranking directions by real importance and choosing how many to keep, just derived through this more general, direct matrix operation instead.
4. A Real, Genuine Advantage for Sparse Data

blocks.alt: SVD works well on sparse data

blocks.text: PCA genuinely requires mean centering the data first, and for a genuinely sparse matrix, like the TF-IDF matrices covered back in Text Features, mostly zeros with only a few nonzero entries per row, centering would genuinely destroy that sparsity, turning nearly every zero into some small nonzero number, and exploding real memory use in the process.

TruncatedSVD, scikit-learn genuine, dedicated tool for this situation, works directly on the original, uncentered matrix, preserving its real sparsity, making it genuinely the appropriate choice for exactly the kind of high dimensional, sparse text data first flagged as a real, practical challenge back in Text Features.

blocks.title: Worth remembering
blocks.content: Never apply plain PCA directly to a genuinely sparse matrix like a TF-IDF representation. TruncatedSVD genuinely exists specifically to handle this exact case without destroying sparsity.

blocks.text: 5. A Worked Example
Applying TruncatedSVD to a small TF-IDF matrix, directly building on the Text Features worked example, shows this sparse data advantage in practice.

code.content:
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer
from sklearn.decomposition import TruncatedSVD

reviews = [
    "Great battery life, would buy again.",
    "Screen cracked after one week, very disappointed.",
    "Great screen, but battery life is short.",
]

tfidf_matrix = TfidfVectorizer(stop_words="english").fit_transform(reviews)

svd = TruncatedSVD(n_components=2, random_state=42)
reduced = svd.fit_transform(tfidf_matrix)

print("Explained variance ratio:", svd.explained_variance_ratio_)
print(reduced)

blocks.text: The genuinely sparse, high dimensional TF-IDF matrix from Text Features, one column per vocabulary word, gets compressed directly into just 2 genuinely dense components here, with no centering step ever applied, preserving that original sparsity throughout the entire computation.

blocks.title: A practical habit
blocks.content: Reach for TruncatedSVD, not plain PCA, whenever the input is genuinely sparse, text vectors, one-hot or hash encoded categorical features, or anything similar produced earlier in this course.

blocks.text: 6. Latent Semantic Analysis: A Named Application to Text

blocks.alt: Text documents run through SVD to produce Latent Semantic Analysis

blocks.text: Applying SVD specifically to a text based matrix like TF-IDF has a genuine, well known name of its own in the field, Latent Semantic Analysis, or LSA. The genuine idea is that the resulting components capture latent, underlying topics or themes within a collection of documents, rather than raw individual word counts.

This is worth knowing specifically because LSA shows up frequently as its own named technique in real, practical text analysis work, even though, as this topic has shown directly, it is genuinely nothing more than TruncatedSVD applied to exactly the TF-IDF representations already covered back in Text Features.
7. SVD Versus PCA: A Direct Comparison

blocks.alt: SVD works on the raw matrix while PCA needs centered data

blocks.text: For genuinely dense, already scaled numeric data, PCA and SVD produce genuinely equivalent results, and PCA remains the more familiar, commonly used interface for that specific case. For genuinely sparse data, high cardinality encoded categories or text representations, TruncatedSVD is genuinely the more appropriate, practical choice, since it avoids the centering step that would otherwise destroy that sparsity.

Holding onto this genuine distinction, dense data favors PCA, sparse data favors TruncatedSVD, is exactly the practical decision this topic equips for, building directly on both this topic and the previous one.

blocks.text: 8. SVD Versus What Comes Next

blocks.alt: SVD is covered here, LDA comes next

blocks.text: PCA and SVD together cover the genuine, foundational linear projection techniques this module opened with, both entirely unsupervised, finding structure purely from the input features themselves, with no regard for any target variable at all. The next topic introduces a genuinely different kind of projection entirely.

LDA, Linear Discriminant Analysis, covered next, is a genuinely supervised projection technique, one that directly uses the target labels to find directions that best separate classes from each other, rather than directions that simply capture the most overall variance.

items: SVD genuinely decomposes any matrix into three pieces: U, Sigma, and V transpose.
PCA is genuinely just SVD applied specifically to mean centered data, not a separate, competing technique.
Singular values genuinely indicate how much real structure each direction captures, paralleling PCA explained variance.
TruncatedSVD genuinely works directly on sparse data, like TF-IDF matrices, without requiring centering first.
Latent Semantic Analysis is a genuinely well known, named application of SVD specifically to text data.
The next topic, LDA, introduces a genuinely supervised projection technique, using target labels directly.
